text:
sam: ops-bot flagged nvme iops spike on eu-west2 GPU fleet, provisioning failing for small jobs. Any eyes?
ops-bot: ALERT: gnode-42/43 nvme_iops>35k, scrub_backlog=12h, gpu_attach_latency=800ms, affected_pods=34
maya: saw that, a few preemptible hosts hit writeback storms. GPUs stuck in 'attaching' loop.
leo: Can we throttle janitor scrub on those hosts? We need to avoid evicting GPUs — draining would be costly.
ingrid: We shipped the scrub rate limiter last week but it didn't include eu-west2 edge pools. I can patch the rule now.
sam: Proposed short plan: pause scrub on pool `eu-west2-scratch-hot` for 2h, reroute new small jobs to `warm-pool-ssd`, and bump the attach timeout to avoid flapping. Tradeoff: extra warm-ssd cost ~ $600/day. Thoughts?
maya: :thumbsup: prefer temporary move vs large-scale drain. How do we pause scrub safely?
ingrid: PATCH commands:```sh
# pause scrub for 2h on that pool
kubectl exec -n infra janitor-ctl -- pause-scrub --pool eu-west2-scratch-hot --duration 2h
# quick sanity check
kubectl logs -n infra janitor-ctl | tail -n 50
```
ops-bot: ACTION: scrub-paused on pool eu-west2-scratch-hot by ingrid at 6300000010
leo: Started routing change: `route-policy set --from=queue-small --to=warm-ssd --if=region==eu-west2` will take ~45s to propagate.
sam: Monitoring: attach latency halved in ~3m, nvme_iops trending back to baseline, GPUs provisioning ramping. Will re-evaluate at +2h.
maya: We should follow up with a longer-term fix: automatic scrub-hedging during high attach latency & constrained GPU supply. RFC?
leo: I'll open an ops ticket and add telemetry/alert: `nvme_iops > 25k && attach_latency > 500ms -> mute_scrub && flip_routing`. Assign to storage team.
ingrid: Added a temporary feature flag: `janitor.rate_limit.euw2 = 0.3`. Deploying canary now.
sam: Nice. Also watch warm-ssd saturation and cost — fallback to degraded cheaper pool if warm-ssd fills.
maya: Thanks team — closing the loop here. If this recurs we'll post a short postmortem in #incidents. :white_check_mark:
